parts.t: Space technology, satellites and launch vehicles
items: India's first orbital computing satellite; uses AI-based data processing in space.
India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle; successful flight under Mission Aagaman on 18 July 2026.
India's first indigenous stratospheric super-pressure balloon; launched from Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.
Described as the world's first commercial, privately operated space station scheduled for development.

Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer (SMILE).
Earth observation satellite launched using GSLV-F17; first Indian satellite to carry out imaging from geosynchronous orbit.

Air-to-surface missile; jointly flight-tested on 2 June 2026.
Long-range surface-to-air air-defence system; tested at APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha.

**What it is:** indigenous automatic train protection system; prevents Signal Passing at Danger and reduces collision risks.
**Key improvements:** improved train-location accuracy, signal information, station communication through optical-fibre cable and electronic interlocking integration.

items: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with NIC and DigiHaat
Enables citizens and organisations to donate verified digital-equipment bundles to eligible Gram Panchayats.
Government of India; developed by March 2026
Integrated digital platform for mapping drinking-water supply infrastructure; digital mapping of water supply systems, from source to household tap.
Nationwide framework to assess Gram Panchayat and traditional local-body performance.
Multilingual, voice-enabled digital public services; supports over 36 languages in text and more than 22 in voice.
GIS-based spatial planning and decision-support platform for Gram Panchayat Development Plans.
Uses AI to convert Gram Sabha and Panchayat meeting recordings into structured minutes.
**Integration:** integrated with Meri Panchayat and DigiHaat.
**Donors:** can choose pre-approved computer bundles mapped to State-specific technical specifications.
Launched on 25 December 2024; first of 30 proposed river-linking projects under the National Perspective Plan.
594-km expressway connecting Meerut and Prayagraj; inaugurated in 2026.

Being developed at Lothal, Gujarat, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
Planned as the world's largest museum at North and South Blocks, Raisina Hill, under Central Vista Redevelopment Project.
Uttar Pradesh plans to develop a 500-acre Japan City in the YEIDA region.

**Region:** addresses water shortages in Bundelkhand across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
**Rivers:** both rivers are tributaries of the Yamuna.
**Phase I:** includes Daudhan Dam and a 216.46-km link canal.
**Phase II:** includes Lower Orr Dam, Kotha Barrage and Bina Complex.

**Flower composition:** approximately 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus.
**Handover:** the Agriculture Department develops the fields and transfers them to selected SHGs and cooperative societies.

lectures.title: Elections 2026: States, world leaders and international bodies

items: **Suvendu Adhikari** became the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal.
**Trinamool Congress:** the result ended its 15-year rule.
All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)
**Chief Minister:** C. Joseph Vijay became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.
**Support:** Vijay secured support of 120 MLAs-elect in the 234-member Assembly.
**Government formation:** received support from Congress, CPI, CPI(M), VCK and IUML.
**Vijay** became the first Tamil Nadu Chief Minister since 1967 who did not belong to either DMK or AIADMK.
**Pro-tem Speaker:** Karuppaiah, elected from Sholavandan, was appointed Pro-tem Speaker.
**Chief Minister:** V.D. Satheesan of the Indian National Congress became Chief Minister.
**Result:** United Democratic Front (UDF) won 102 of 140 seats.
**Alliance:** the Indian National Congress was the principal party within the UDF alliance.
**Oath:** the Chief Minister took oath on 18 May 2026.

parts.t: Presidents elected or sworn in around the world
items: Began his second five-year term; sworn in 1 September 2026.
Re-elected for a sixth presidential term; 97.81% votes, 10 April 2026.

items: Former Bulgarian President, elected Prime Minister of Bulgaria; elected 8 May 2026.
Assumed office for a third consecutive term as Denmark's Prime Minister; 3 June 2026.
Sworn in February 2026; the youngest-ever and first openly gay Prime Minister of the Netherlands.
Designated as 105th PM; Japan's first woman (female) Prime Minister.
Elected 2 June 2026; defeated Andreas Kakouris of Cyprus.

Chief Election Commissioner; represented India as Chair.

parts.t: India in international bodies: FATF, IMO, UNESCO, International IDEA
items: **India** was elected FATF Vice-President for the first time in June 2026.
**Vivek Aggarwal:** appointed as India's FATF Vice-President; tenure July 2026 to June 2027.
**Giles Thomson:** named as the next FATF President from 1 July 2026.
**India:** re-elected to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Council for the 2026–27 biennium.
**Category:** B. Category B comprises 10 countries with the largest interest in international seaborne trade.
**India:** re-elected to UNESCO's Executive Board for the 2025–29 term.
**Deepavali:** inscription on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
**India:** assumed chairship of the Council of Member States for 2026.
**Founding member:** India is a founding member of International IDEA.
**Vice-Chairs:** Mauritius and Mexico served as Vice-Chairs alongside India.
**Membership:** International IDEA has 35 Member States and two Observers.
**Theme:** “Democracy for an Inclusive, Peaceful, Resilient and Sustainable World.”
Interim President; first Indian to serve in this role

lectures.title: Important visits and India's bilateral visits, 2025-26

items: Visited with PM Modi; participated in Ganga Aarti. The visit strengthened cultural cooperation between Varanasi and Kyoto.
Attended the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit; main meeting with PM Modi was on 2 July.
Visited the Mahabodhi Temple and offered prayers during a three-day state visit to India.
Described as his first official visit to the disputed islands.
Visited Tamil Nadu and inaugurated a section of Chennai Metro Rail Phase II.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 29–30 August 2026; State visit at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
**India–Uzbekistan:** Strategic Partnership upgraded to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
**Award:** Uzbekistan conferred its highest state award, Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik Order, on Modi.
**Discussed:** long-term uranium supply, peaceful nuclear energy, geological exploration, mining and mineral processing.
**UPI:** NPCI International Payments Ltd. and Uzbekistan’s National Interbank Processing Centre agreed to enable Indian UPI apps to scan Uzbekistan’s UZQR codes.
**Joint military exercise:** DUSTLIK, 7th edition, held in Namangan Region in April 2026.
**MoU:** an MoU on Ayurveda and traditional medicines was signed.
**Scholarships:** India announced 100 Lal Bahadur Shastri Hindi Scholarships and an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.
**Grant:** a US$1 million grant was announced for ecological rehabilitation in the Aral Sea region.

parts.t: Myanmar: President U Min Aung Hlaing in India
items: **Visit:** President U Min Aung Hlaing, 30 May–3 June 2026; first foreign trip since assuming office.
**Bodh Gaya:** visited Mahabodhi Temple, Mahabodhi Meditation Centre and Sujata Temple.
**NETRA:** visited NTPC’s Energy Technology Research Alliance (NETRA), Greater Noida.
**Policies:** cooperation discussed under India’s Neighbourhood First and Act East policies.
**Connectivity projects discussed:** Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project and India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway.
**Scholarships:** India announced an increase in Mekong-Ganga ICCR scholarships for Myanmar students from 36 to 100.
Cyprus: President Nikos Christodoulides in India
**Visit:** President Nikos Christodoulides, 20–23 May 2026; first visit to India in his current capacity.
**India–Cyprus** relations elevated to a Strategic Partnership.
**Programme:** held talks with PM Modi, met President Droupadi Murmu, paid homage at Rajghat and participated in a Business Forum in Mumbai.
**Anniversary:** 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations to be commemorated in 2027.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 27–29 June 2026; second visit after March 2015.
**Occasion:** visit coincided with the 50th anniversary of Seychelles’ independence and diplomatic relations with India.
**SESEL:** cooperation advanced under the Joint Vision for Sustainability, Economic Growth and Security through Enhanced Linkages (SESEL).
**Gifts from India:** Fast Patrol Vessel PS Lespwar, ten utility vehicles, five sets of sailing boats, six ambulances, 500 metric tonnes of rice and 8,500 metric tonnes of cement.
**CDRI:** Seychelles decided to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.
**UPI:** NPCI International Payments Ltd. and the Central Bank of Seychelles signed an MoU on UPI implementation.
PM Modi in the UAE, 15 May 2026
**Visit:** official visit as part of a five-nation tour covering UAE, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy.
**Meeting:** met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi.
**Strategic petroleum reserves:** potential ADNOC crude-oil storage of up to 30 million barrels, including Visakhapatnam and Chandikhol facilities.
**LPG:** Indian Oil Corporation and ADNOC signed a Strategic Collaboration Agreement on LPG supplies.
**Ship repair:** Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World agreed to develop a ship-repair cluster at Vadinar.
**Supercomputing:** C-DAC and G42 discussed an 8-exaflop supercomputing cluster.
**Trade:** Virtual Trade Corridor using MAITRI was also welcomed.
**Visit:** President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, 19 January 2026.
**Dholera:** LoI on UAE participation in Dholera Special Investment Region, Gujarat.
**NIIF:** investment in the second NIIF Infrastructure Fund discussed.
**LNG:** HPCL and ADNOC Gas signed a 10-year agreement for 0.5 million metric tonnes per annum of LNG from 2028.
**Other initiatives mentioned:** IN-SPACe–UAE Space Agency collaboration, proposed Strategic Defence Partnership Framework and House of India museum in Abu Dhabi.
Switzerland: President Guy Parmelin in India
**Programme:** visited Rajghat, held talks with PM Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House and met President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
**Five agreements/arrangements:** migration and mobility, young professionals’ exchange, transport technology, research cooperation and innovation implementation.
**Young Professionals Exchange Agreement:** provides for 300 professionals annually from each country, expandable to 500.
**India–EFTA TEPA:** signed on 10 March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025.
**TEPA target:** US$100 billion investment and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years.
**No separate leader visit:** India–UK CETA and Double Contribution Convention (DCC) became operational on 15 July 2026.

parts.t: Norway and Italy: PM Modi's visits
items: **Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, Oslo, 18–19 May 2026; focused on bilateral relations, climate, clean energy and Arctic cooperation.
**Summit:** Oslo hosted the 3rd India–Nordic Summit on 19 May 2026.
**India–Nordic** relations elevated to a trusted Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership.
**Cooperation:** renewable energy, green hydrogen, Arctic research and the Himadri research station at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 19–20 May 2026; met PM Giorgia Meloni and President Sergio Mattarella in Rome.
**India–Italy** relations upgraded to a Special Strategic Partnership.
**Cooperation:** defence, counterterrorism, space, technology and IMEC.
**Initiatives:** INNOVIT India and ICI–Italy Calls India.
**Honour:** Modi received the FAO Agricola Medal at FAO headquarters in Rome.

parts.t: France and Germany: leaders in India
items: **India–France** relations upgraded to a Special Global Strategic Partnership under the Horizon 2047 Roadmap.
**India–France Year of Innovation 2026:** inaugurated in Mumbai, focusing on AI, science, healthcare, research and education.
**Tata–Airbus H125 Final Assembly Line:** at Vemagal, Karnataka, described as India’s first private-sector helicopter final assembly line.
**HAMMER missiles:** BEL and Safran signed a joint-venture MoU to manufacture HAMMER missiles in India.
**Energy:** cooperation also covered nuclear energy and renewable energy.
**Visit:** Chancellor Friedrich Merz, 12–13 January 2026; visited India and held talks with PM Narendra Modi in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
**Cooperation:** trade, defence, technology, clean energy and migration.
**Visa:** Germany announced visa-free airport transit for Indian passport holders, effective 3 June 2026.
**Joint Declaration of Intent:** on Global Skills Partnership, ethical recruitment and cooperation against irregular migration and human trafficking.
**Skilling:** a renewable-energy skilling Centre of Excellence was proposed at the National Skill Training Institute, Hyderabad.

parts.t: President Murmu in Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania
items: Described as the first visit by an Indian President to **Moldova** and **North Macedonia**, and the first to **Romania** since May 1994.
**Moldova:** cooperation in agriculture, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, DPI and AI.
**North Macedonia:** President Murmu met President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova and addressed the Assembly.
**North Macedonia talks:** discussions included trade and pharmaceutical manufacturing.
**Skopje:** Gandhi bust unveiled in Skopje; visit to Mother Teresa Memorial mentioned.
**Romania:** India and Romania agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade over the next three years and strengthening defence cooperation.

parts.t: North America and South America: Canada and Brazil
items: Canada: PM Mark Carney in India
**Visit:** PM Mark Carney, 27 February–2 March 2026; major turning point in India–Canada relations.
**Uranium:** Cameco–Department of Atomic Energy agreement of approximately CAD 2.6 billion for long-term uranium supply to India.
**Centre of Excellence:** proposed Canada–India Pulse Protein Centre of Excellence at NIFTEM Kundli.
**AICTE–Mitacs MoU:** to support around 300 Indian undergraduate research internships annually from 2027.
**Trade target:** long-term bilateral trade target of approximately CAD 70 billion by 2030.
**Visit:** President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 18–22 February 2026.
**Programme:** attended India AI Impact Summit 2026 and held bilateral talks with PM Modi on 21 February in New Delhi.
**Count:** this was Lula’s fifth visit to India as President and sixth visit overall.
**Outcome:** bilateral ties elevated to a strategic level; trade target of over US$30 billion by 2030.
**MoU:** on mining and minerals for the steel sector.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 16–17 December 2025; first bilateral visit to Ethiopia.
**Programme:** held talks with PM Abiy Ahmed Ali and addressed a joint session of the Ethiopian Parliament.
**Award:** Modi received Ethiopia’s highest award, Great Honour Nishan of Ethiopia.
**India and Ethiopia** agreed to elevate ties to a Strategic Partnership.
**Historical connection:** trade during the Axumite Empire through Adulis port; formal diplomatic relations established in 1950.
**Liberia:** India and Liberia launched the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers at UN Headquarters, New York, on 25 September 2026.
**Mali:** First India–Mali Forum for the Promotion of Exports held in Bamako on 19–20 June 2026.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 8–10 July 2026; attended the Third Australia–India Annual Summit in Melbourne on 9 July.
**Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap:** covered maritime-domain awareness, surveillance, information exchange, operational coordination, search and rescue, and sea-lane protection.
**MoU:** between Indian Coast Guard and Australia’s Maritime Border Command on maritime law enforcement and border protection.
**Support:** Australia supported India’s NSG membership and Gaganyaan.
**Uranium:** uranium exports for peaceful use under IAEA safeguards were discussed.
**Visit:** PM Narendra Modi, 10–11 July 2026; visit to Auckland.
First Indian prime-ministerial visit to **New Zealand** in four decades.
**Outcome:** India and New Zealand established a Strategic Partnership, adopted the Roadmap to 2030 and concluded ten agreements/arrangements.
